questions.question: During the on-road driving test, what must you NOT do?

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic laws.
Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road driving test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, following all traffic laws, and completing the test without accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: What tool checks if tires have the right air pressure?

options.text: A tire gauge
A tire iron
An air compressor
A lug nut

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, use a tire gauge to check tire air pressure. Kicking the tires is not acceptable.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, what must you NOT do?

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals, follow all traffic laws, and avoid accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: If a school bus catches fire, what should happen to the students?

options.text: They must leave the bus.
They should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
They should stay in their seats.

questions.explanation: If a school bus is on fire or might catch fire, the bus driver must get all students off the bus right away.

questions.question: If you must drive during strong winds, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: School buses can be pushed by wind because of their large sides. In windy conditions, grip the steering wheel firmly, expect wind gusts, and reduce your speed. Contact your dispatcher if you need help deciding whether to continue driving.

questions.question: When checking tires during the vehicle inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: More wear on the inside of the tires than the outside.
More wear on the outside of the tires than the inside.
More wear in the middle of the tires than the outside.
Even wear across all tires.

questions.explanation: When checking your tires during the vehicle inspection test, make sure the tread is worn evenly.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror in a school bus used for?

options.text: To watch the passengers inside the bus.
To see hazards on the road ahead.
To see vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch the passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror in a school bus lets the driver see what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, after crossing a bridge, what might you be asked to recall?

options.text: The posted weight limit.
The color of a sign you passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
If there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.explanation: The examiner may ask you to recall the weight limit posted on a bridge you just crossed during the on-road driving skills test.

questions.question: With properly adjusted mirrors, a school bus driver can see how far behind the bus?

options.text: One bus length
Two bus lengths
Three bus lengths
Four bus lengths

questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is critical for safe school bus operation. The flat mirrors should be adjusted so you can see 200 feet, or four bus lengths, behind the bus.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks during the driving test, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Stop
Pass slower vehicles.
Change lanes.
Put the vehicle in neutral.

questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during the on-road driving skills test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts should be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.explanation: Lug nuts must be present and tight. They should have no cracks, no distortions, and no rust. Check that all bolt holes are also free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: Where should you park your vehicle at the end of the test?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
Within five feet of where the examiner instructed.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of where the examiner instructed.

questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner told you to use. You will lose points if you do not follow the examiner's instructions exactly. This is important for passing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver does not show up for their basic skills test.
Your vehicle touches an exercise boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one section of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle touches an exercise boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the basic skills test. Each encroachment counts as one error.

questions.question: When you perform the stop/start maneuver during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to get onto the shoulder.
Not use any turn signals.
Slam on the brakes to stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down smoothly.

questions.explanation: To perform the stop/start maneuver, check traffic, signal your turn, and slow down with smooth, even braking. Change gears as needed. Come to a full stop without coasting.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus because of a hazard, a driver should:

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the hazard and decide how to respond.
Tell students to panic.
Have students open all the windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the hazard and decide how to respond.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer staying on the bus. If you have time, contact your dispatcher to report the emergency. Then decide together whether to evacuate.

questions.question: When driving a school bus and you reach railroad tracks, you should generally:

options.text: Check the tracks but keep driving without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings. Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail to see the tracks clearly. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are present.
Check traffic only in the direction of the turn.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.explanation: Before turning, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: When driving on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Switch lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On an expressway, keep proper lane position, spacing, and speed. Check your mirrors often to see all traffic around you.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space.

questions.question: Once you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Keep the vehicle in first gear.
Be perpendicular to the curb.
Be blocking a driveway.

questions.explanation: Apply the parking brake when you stop. Shift to neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block any driveways or intersections.
